content.value_statement: Survival analysis is difficult when outcomes are censored and metrics differ from standard regression. This skill guides scikit-survival workflows from data setup to model evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Cox, ensemble, SVM, nonparametric, and competing risks methods.
Shows how to create structured survival outcomes from arrays or data frames.
Guides preprocessing for missing values, categorical variables, scaling, and train-test splits.
Covers C-index, IPCW C-index, time-dependent AUC, and Brier score selection.
Provides reference guidance for hyperparameter tuning with scikit-learn tools.
Highlights common pitfalls for censored data and competing event types.
limitations: It is documentation guidance, not an executable package or installed Python dependency.
It does not validate statistical assumptions on a user dataset automatically.
It does not replace clinical, regulatory, or domain expert review.
Examples may need adjustment for local scikit-survival versions and data schemas.

use_cases.title: Plan a Survival Modeling Workflow
use_cases.description: Choose data preparation, model families, and metrics for censored time-to-event data.

use_cases.title: Compare Survival Model Families
use_cases.description: Assess Cox, ensemble, SVM, and nonparametric methods for a project goal.

use_cases.title: Review Survival Evaluation Choices
use_cases.description: Select appropriate C-index, AUC, and Brier score methods for censoring conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare censored survival data and choose a first scikit-survival model.

prompt_templates.title: Select Evaluation Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Given my censoring rate and prediction goal, recommend survival metrics and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a comparison of Cox, Random Survival Forest, gradient boosting, and Survival SVM models.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complete Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my survival analysis plan for leakage, censoring errors, metric misuse, and competing risks issues.

output_examples.input: I have right-censored patient follow-up data and need a baseline model.
output_examples.output: A recommended workflow with survival outcome creation, Cox model setup, preprocessing checks, and appropriate C-index evaluation.

output_examples.input: My dataset has high censoring and I am using Harrell C-index.
output_examples.output: Guidance to consider Uno IPCW C-index, define evaluation times, and report censoring-aware performance.

output_examples.input: Events include relapse and death without relapse.
output_examples.output: A competing risks framing that explains cumulative incidence and warns against treating all competing events as simple censoring.

best_practices: Start with clear event definitions, censoring rules, and follow-up time units.
Use train-only preprocessing and censoring-aware metrics during validation.
Compare interpretable and flexible models before selecting a final approach.
anti_patterns: Treating censored observations as ordinary negative labels.
Using standard regression metrics for time-to-event predictions.
Ignoring competing risks when event types prevent each other.

faq.question: Does this skill install scikit-survival?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You must manage Python packages in your environment.

faq.question: Can it handle censored data?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance centers on censored time-to-event outcomes and scikit-survival data structures.

faq.question: Which models are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Cox models, penalized Cox, survival ensembles, Survival SVMs, nonparametric estimators, and competing risks basics.

faq.question: Does it provide medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports statistical modeling workflows and does not replace expert medical review.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: How should I evaluate model performance?
faq.answer: Use censoring-aware metrics such as IPCW C-index, time-dependent AUC, and integrated Brier score when appropriate.
